answer: A deposit bond makes each agent identity costly to create. A new agent locks a small stake, like an opal held in escrow, before it can trade or vote. A sybil operator who wants a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits, and the cost rises faster than the gain. Bad behavior loses the deposit. Like water carving a canyon, the rule slowly wears down cheap copies until only agents with real work and real stake remain, and repeated offenses push the cost into a spiral that fake identities cannot afford to climb.
